title: LedgerLoop: pricing an AI bookkeeping feature
prompt: Our client is LedgerLoop, which sells accounting software to small businesses. It has built an AI assistant that categorizes expenses automatically. How should LedgerLoop price the new feature?

clarifying_answers.objective: Maximize profit from the feature without hurting customer retention.
clarifying_answers.customers: Small businesses with 1 to 20 employees, in the US.
clarifying_answers.options: Open to bundling it into the base plan or selling it as a paid add-on.

hidden_facts.hint: the customer base or current pricing
hidden_facts.fact: LedgerLoop has 50,000 customers (in thousands: 50) paying $40 a month.

hidden_facts.hint: how much time or money the feature saves
hidden_facts.fact: Pilot customers saved about 3 hours a month on bookkeeping. Small-business owners value their time at roughly $50 an hour.

hidden_facts.hint: what the feature costs to run
hidden_facts.fact: Each customer's AI usage costs LedgerLoop about $2 a month in model and server costs.

hidden_facts.hint: competitors or how others price similar features
hidden_facts.fact: QuickBooks includes a similar feature in its $90-a-month plan. Xero charges a $15-a-month add-on.

hidden_facts.hint: willingness to pay, surveys, or adoption at different prices
hidden_facts.fact: In a survey, 40% of customers would add the feature at $10 a month, and 20% at $20 a month.

exhibits.title: Customers who would buy, by monthly price (%)

math_answers.question: How much is the feature worth to a typical customer each month?
What monthly profit does the feature make at $10?
What monthly profit does the feature make at $20?

ideal_structure: Three pricing lenses: cost, competitors, customer value
Competitor anchors: Xero add-on, QuickBooks bundle
Value ceiling: hours saved x value of time
Profit at each price point; retention and strategic effects
recommendation: Sell it as an add-on at about $15 a month, between the two tested prices and matching Xero. $20 makes slightly more profit than $10 ($180K vs $160K a month) but reaches only half as many customers, and the feature is worth about $150 a month to users, so the price leaves them plenty of value. Then test a higher-priced plan that bundles the feature.
common_mistakes: Picking the highest-profit price without thinking about adoption and retention
